one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window, both on 2026-10-15. First, the South32 AGM vote on the AliGroup sale at 12:00 AWST, before the US open. The independent expert calls the deal fair and reasonable and the board recommends it unanimously, so it very likely passes; that is a small positive because it removes deal-break risk. Second, Alcoa's Q3 2026 results after the close, with the call at 5pm EDT. Guidance was small sequential items only (Alumina +$10M, Section 232 cost -$10M, alumina cost in the Aluminum segment -$10M). Price effects are negative: LME is about $3,200-3,300 against a higher Q2 average, and the Midwest premium is $1.09/lb, off its $1.19 June peak. Consensus EPS has drifted to about $1.46 (from about $1.52, vs $2.12 in Q2), so the drop is well flagged. The bigger swing factor is Q4 and 2027 commentary on the premium, the Canada tariff, the Gulf restart (EGA full by Q1 2027) and alumina. I have no directional edge, so the forecast stays centred on $42 at about 17% one-month vol (56%/3.5 = 16%, widened slightly for the earnings day). The ladder is unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Pro forma, because the AliGroup deal is expected to close in H1 2027, before the horizon. (a) 5.25x normalized combined EBITDA of $3.1B (standalone $2.3B + AliGroup $0.78B + partial synergies) = EV $16.3B, less about $3.15B of net claims at Sep-2027 (net debt $4.75B + pension/OPEB $0.57B - Ma'aden $1.25B - FCF $0.9B), over 282M diluted shares = $46.5. (b) normalized EPS of about $4.30 x 10.5x = $45. Blended 60/40 = $46.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Normalized combined EBITDA $3.1B x 5.25x = EV $16.3B; less net claims at Sep-2027 of about $3.15B ($5.42B debt - $0.67B cash + $0.57B pension/OPEB - $1.25B Ma'aden stake - $0.9B FCF Jul-26 to Sep-27); equity $13.1B / 282M diluted shares = $46.5

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 adj. EBITDA ex special items was $1,965M (src 4) at about $2,630/t LME. My deck is about $2,900/t in 2027: below the forward curve near $3,200-3,250, above Goldman's cut to $2,700 (src 17). The Midwest premium is about $1.0-1.09/lb (CFO, src 9). At the supervisor's checked sensitivity of about $0.2B per $100/t, that adds about +$0.5B. I take back about $0.15B for alumina weakness (segment -$96M in Q2, src 1) and Pinjarra costs, giving $2.3B. LTM to Jun-26 was $2,293M at much higher Q2 prices (src 4), so $2.3B is not a peak number only because 2025-26 alumina was a drag.

South32 memorandum: about $0.8B average underlying EBITDA FY21-FY25 (src 7). The offering memorandum implies about $0.85-0.86B for FY2025 and LTM Jun-26 (src 4). Trimmed slightly for my below-spot price deck.

inputs_detail.input: Synergies (partial in the year to Sep-2027)
inputs_detail.derivation: Management guides about $50M run-rate within the first year after closing. With an H1 2027 close, only part is in the run-rate by the horizon.

Alcoa is paying about 6.8x through-cycle for AliGroup (src 7), which caps the range. I discount for leverage that rises to about 1x normalized EBITDA, a loss-making alumina segment in 2026 (src 1) and commodity cyclicality. Cut from 5.5x in round 1 to stay consistent with 10.5x P/E at this leverage.
Pro forma total debt $5,420M (src 4) less pro forma cash $668M (src 16). In round 1 I assumed $0.85B of cash; the pro forma balance sheet shows $668M.
$573M at 30-Jun-2026, included by Alcoa in adjusted net debt (Q2 release net debt table). Omitted in round 1.
$1,360M carried on the Q2 and pro forma balance sheets. I haircut about 8% for mark-to-market and tax/liquidity friction on any sale.

inputs_detail.input: FCF Jul-2026 to Sep-2027 after dividends and ticking fee
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 FCF was $422M at peak prices (src 1). At a mid-cycle deck I assume about $200-250M per quarter for 5 quarters (the AliGroup contribution starts after closing), less dividends of about $0.03B per quarter, the $80-100M ticking fee (src 8), and interest on the new notes (pro forma interest about $0.39B per year, src 16).
Pro forma diluted 282.8M: 263.8M basic plus 17,008,960 consideration shares plus dilutive awards (src 16).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Normalized pro forma EPS about $4.30 x 10.5x = $45

inputs_detail.derivation: EBITDA $3.1B less pro forma D&A $0.92B (FY2025 pro forma $916M, src 16) less interest about $0.39B (FY2025 pro forma $395M, src 16) = $1.79B pretax; tax at about 32% gives about $1.22B. Cross-check: pro forma LTM net income was $1,482M ($5.27/share) at Hormuz-peak pricing (src 4).
Alcoa's mix is high-tax Australia and Brazil, while US and Spain losses carry valuation allowances, so the effective rate sits above 30%.
A mid-cycle multiple on already-normalized EPS, so there is no double haircut. Consistent with 5.25x EV/EBITDA at about 1x leverage. Below the sell-side target-implied 11-12x on $5+ EPS (src 11).

bear.story: The Gulf restart completes (EGA full by Q1 2027) and the 2027 surplus widens. LME falls to about $2,500-2,600/t, below Goldman's $2,700. A US-Canada deal cuts the 232 tariff and the Midwest premium falls well below $0.80/lb. Alumina stays below $350/t and WA approval delays hit Pinjarra/Huntly. Combined EBITDA is about $2.3B at 4.5-5x, against about $3.3B of net claims after the Ma'aden credit.

base.story: LME holds at $2,800-3,100 and the Midwest premium stays near $1.0/lb, because the US must still import about 1Mt beyond Canada (CFO). The restarts run at full rate. AliGroup closes in H1 2027 and contributes about $0.78B EBITDA, and combined EBITDA runs about $3.1B. Deleveraging plus the Ma'aden asset support about 5.25x, or $46.

bull.story: The forward curve near $3,200-3,300 holds as the Gulf restart slips or demand surprises, and tariffs persist with the premium at $1.09/lb or higher. Combined EBITDA reaches about $3.7B, and at 5.5x less about $2.9B of net claims gives about $62. Faster deleveraging and possible buybacks add a little more. I no longer cite WoodMac/CRU $3,500+ forecasts; this case rests only on spot and forward levels.

thesis_break_reason: At $27, pro forma equity (282M diluted shares) is about $7.6B. With about $3.2-3.5B of net claims after the pension and the Ma'aden credit, that implies EV of about $11B, roughly 3.5x my $3.1B normalized combined EBITDA, which is well below the 6.8x Alcoa is paying for AliGroup. That level would most likely mean something structural: LME heading to $2,500 with the Midwest premium collapsing after tariff removal, failure of the AliGroup deal or of the WA bauxite approvals, or leverage breaching management's 2.0x cap. Ordinary aluminium-price noise would not take it there.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks, which I verified in the pro forma 8-K Ex.99.3 and the Q2 release net debt table, changed three inputs. (1) Pro forma cash is $668M, not my assumed $0.85B, and the $573M net pension/OPEB, which Alcoa itself counts in adjusted net debt, belongs in net claims; together about -$2.7/share. (2) My $2.0B standalone mid-cycle EBITDA was FY2025's level at about $2,630 LME, which is inconsistent with my own $2,900 deck. Lifting it to $2.3B adds about +$5/share at 5.25x. (3) I dropped the unsourced WoodMac/CRU $3,500+ claim and added Goldman's 2027 cut to $2,700, which lowers my bull case to $65 and trims the far-right tail. I also moved to 5.25x EV/EBITDA, consistent with 10.5x P/E at about 1x leverage. Ex.99.3 gives D&A $916M and interest $395M, so normalized EPS is about $4.30. Result: EV/EBITDA $46.5 and P/E $45, blended $46 (round 1 $45), about 10% above spot. I still sit below the sell-side's roughly $60 average, which embeds 2026 peak pricing and mostly standalone EPS of about $5.7-6.0. Distribution: roughly lognormal with a median of about $44.5 and 48% vol (below the 56% realized vol, because the June spike/unwind inflates it), plus a fatter left tail for post-deal leverage. Scenarios are $26/$46/$65 at 25/50/25%, a mean of about $45.8. Ladder changes are small: +0.5 pt at $42-46 from the higher fair value, and -0.3 to -0.5 pt at $84-105 from the lower bull case. The Q3 consensus slipping to $1.46 does not change the neutral one-month view.
